findings.description: Aftermarket tank grip pads (traction pads) installed on both sides of the fuel tank. These are non-OEM rubber/silicone grip panels, commonly used on sport bikes for knee grip during aggressive riding. Appears to be a Kawasaki ZX-series or similar inline-4 sportbike.
findings.location_in_image: Both sides of fuel tank, mid-frame

findings.description: Aftermarket shorty/adjustable brake lever visible on right handlebar. Non-OEM lever with adjustable reach, appears to be a performance aftermarket unit (possibly Pazzo, Driven, or similar brand).
Aftermarket clutch lever installed on left handlebar — appears to be a shorty adjustable lever matching the brake lever, suggesting a matched set of aftermarket controls.
Aftermarket windscreen/windshield installed — appears to be a tinted/smoked double-bubble or tall sport screen, replacing the OEM unit. Appears in good condition with no visible cracks.
Aftermarket frame sliders/crash bungs visible on lower frame rails. Black cylindrical sliders mounted to the lower fairing bracket area — a common track/street modification for crash protection.

Entire motorcycle appears to have been repainted or wrapped in a uniform light gray/silver color. The paint appears fresh and glossy with no visible OEM decals or graphics, suggesting a full respray or vinyl wrap. This could indicate prior damage repair.

Fuel tank cap/filler area shows discoloration and appears weathered or faded compared to the surrounding freshly painted tank surface. The cap ring appears oxidized/aged, inconsistent with a fresh paint job — may indicate the tank was repainted but the cap was not replaced.

Rear tire visible in later frames shows tread present but image blur limits detailed assessment. Tread pattern appears to be a sport/performance tire. No obvious flat spots, cracking, or extreme wear visible, but a hands-on inspection is recommended.
findings.location_in_image: Rear wheel area, lower right of frame

findings.description: Rider seat shows moderate wear — the vinyl surface appears slightly faded and worn smooth in the center seating area. No visible tears or cracks, but the seat cover shows use consistent with moderate mileage.
Passenger seat/rear cowl area shows similar wear to the main seat — surface appears worn and slightly faded. Consistent with normal use.

Exhaust header pipes visible at the rear of the engine show bronze/golden discoloration consistent with heat cycling and mild surface oxidation. This is typical for used exhaust systems but indicates the bike has been ridden. No heavy rust or pitting visible.

Multiple loose fasteners/hardware (bolts, screws) observed on the lift table surface next to the motorcycle in later frames. This indicates the bike is partially disassembled or in the process of reassembly. Some fasteners appear to be small body/fairing screws. Technician should verify all fasteners are accounted for and properly torqued.
findings.location_in_image: Lift table surface, left side of motorcycle

findings.description: Rear license plate bracket/tail section hardware appears to be partially removed or absent in some frames. The tail section area shows exposed mounting points consistent with disassembly in progress.

A small amber/orange indicator light is visible illuminated on or near the instrument cluster area in two frames (top-down tank view). This could be a fuel warning light, check engine light, or other warning indicator. The ignition appears to be in the ON position during this inspection. Requires closer investigation to identify which warning lamp is active.
findings.location_in_image: Instrument cluster / top of tank area, center-left

findings.description: Aftermarket bar-end weights or bar-end mirrors appear to have been removed or replaced — the handlebar ends show aftermarket plugs/caps rather than OEM bar ends.

findings.overall_assessment: This appears to be a sport bike (likely a Kawasaki ZX-series, Suzuki GSX-R, or similar inline-4 supersport) currently on a motorcycle lift in a shop environment undergoing service or inspection. The bike has been extensively modified with aftermarket controls, tank grips, windscreen, and frame sliders. Most notably, the entire motorcycle appears to have received a fresh gray/silver respray or vinyl wrap, which warrants investigation into prior accident history or damage repair. The bike is partially disassembled with loose fasteners on the lift table. An amber warning light was observed illuminated in the instrument cluster area during the walkthrough, which is a priority concern requiring identification. No fluid leaks, smoke, or obvious structural damage were detected in the visible frames. Overall cosmetic condition of the fresh paint is good, but the combination of a full respray, aftermarket modifications, and an active warning light suggests this bike has a history that should be thoroughly investigated before return to service.
suggested_diagnostics: Identify and diagnose the amber/orange warning indicator light observed illuminated in the instrument cluster — pull fault codes with a compatible OBD/diagnostic tool (e.g., KiPass, Healtech GIpro, or dealer tool)
Perform a full VIN history check to investigate prior accident, salvage, or total-loss records — the full respray is a significant red flag
Inspect all fairing and body panel mounting points for signs of prior crash damage, repaired cracks, or misaligned panels hidden under the new paint/wrap
Verify all loose fasteners on the lift table are catalogued and reinstalled to OEM torque specifications before returning the bike to service
Perform a complete chain inspection (stretch, lubrication, sprocket wear) — chain was not clearly visible in the frames provided
Inspect front and rear brake pads for thickness and glazing — brake components were partially obscured in available frames
Check front fork seals for oil weeping — fork tubes were visible but blur prevented detailed assessment
Perform a tire pressure check and close-up tread depth measurement on both front and rear tires
Inspect all cable routing (throttle, clutch, brake lines) for proper routing, kinking, or chafing after reassembly
Verify coolant level and inspect radiator hoses for condition — cooling system components were not clearly visible in the provided frames
Check oil level via sight glass or dipstick and inspect for any leaks around the engine cases
findings.image_quality_note: Significant motion blur affects the majority of frames — approximately 60-70% of frames are too blurry for fine-detail analysis. This limits the ability to assess chain condition, brake pad thickness, fork seal condition, and precise gauge readings. Static, close-up photography of key components (chain, brakes, forks, instrument cluster) is strongly recommended for a complete diagnostic assessment.
